direction.problem: A passenger on a reversing support passes through platform velocity zero while deceleration/reversal acceleration is still active. Zero speed must not be misread as zero load, rest, or a phase-reset cue.

pocket_rule: ZERO SPEED IS A SAMPLE, NOT A REST. IF ACCELERATION STILL OWNS THE LOAD, KEEP THE COUNTERLEAN THROUGH THE TURNAROUND.

history.correction: Deepen K01-K05 chest/pelvis shear, counterbalanced arm reach, front-contact pressure and leg compression while keeping both support contacts present; make K04/K05 preserve peak forward load across velocity zero, then author K06 release and K07 countercatch.
history.highest_value_visible_defect: The first render left the body as a timid stick-figure tilt; platform arrows/labels carried too much of the turnaround read, so zero-speed load continuity was not owned strongly enough by silhouette and support pressure.

history.visible_read: K01-K03 visibly shear chest/pelvis and load the front contact as rightward platform speed falls; K04 reaches v=0 with the same peak loaded silhouette and both contacts still planted; K05 has negative platform velocity while forward load visibly persists; only K06 acceleration release starts body restack; K07 countercatch pays secondary lag before K08 reverse-cruise balance.

noodle_queen.judgment: The useful cruelty is at K04: the platform is momentarily still and the body refuses to pretend that means rest. K05 crosses into reverse travel while keeping the same load story, then the body earns recovery only after acceleration releases. The support graph stays boring on purpose while the silhouette does the physics.
